reference.source: Dhingra Diseases of ENT 8th Edition (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: Intranasal steroid first line for allergic rhinitis and polyps
Polyps are pale insensate; turbinates pink sensitive
Samter triad: polyps, asthma, aspirin sensitivity
Unilateral nasal mass needs tumour exclusion
reference.pathophysiology: Type 2 eosinophilic inflammation oedematously prolapses ethmoid mucosa into polyps in most Western disease, while IgE mast cell activation drives allergic symptoms; ostiomeatal obstruction then stagnates sinus mucus perpetuating infection and inflammation.
additionalDifferentials: Allergic versus vasomotor rhinitis by itch, sneeze and triggers
Polyp versus hypertrophied turbinate by colour and sensation
Antrochoanal (unilateral, youth) versus ethmoid polyps (bilateral, adult)
additionalInvestigations: CT paranasal sinuses for chronic sinusitis surgical planning
Allergy testing when immunotherapy considered; smell testing
